notes: An admin can now hide any field on the self-service (mobile) page, and hiding one actually prevents editing it. Settings in the Clients tab grows from one switch to ten, one per field, all off by default: Proxy, WebRTC, Internet, device Name, IP type, Mode, Local IP, Group, Scan and Bandwidth. The switch that already existed only hid Mode from the screen -- mobile_hide_mode_enabled was read in exactly two places, both building the payload sent down to the page, while the save path applied mode straight from the request without consulting it. /api/public/self needs no login (it identifies a device by its IP alone), so anyone who could open the page could send the request directly and change Mode, while the setting's own description promised they could not. Hidden fields are now stripped from the request body before anything reads it. They are stripped rather than rejected, because the page submits the whole form on every save including untouched fields. The two rotate buttons never went through the form and needed their own guards: the rotate-IP button sits beside the Internet field and only appears for PPPoE, and one press drops every device sharing that session for a few seconds -- both endpoints now refuse with 403 when their field is hidden, and both buttons read the hidden set themselves since they are re-shown after the hide pass. Hiding also does not leave holes: half-hidden rows go single-column, fully hidden rows disappear, and the proxy card and "other options" block vanish once empty.
